social.author: Joseph Borroto
social.headline: I treat the camera like a client, not a camera. That one shift changed all my content.
social.cta: Here's exactly how I do it →

slides.title: Talk TO one person
slides.body: Not 'hey guys.' One person, one problem. It reads as a real conversation.

slides.title: Say the point in line one
slides.body: If the first sentence doesn't stop the scroll, nothing after it matters.

slides.title: Be yourself on camera
slides.body: The personality is the moat. Nobody can copy how you actually talk.

slides.title: Make every video different
slides.body: Same energy, new angle. The feed should never feel like a rerun.

slides.title: Just get content out
slides.body: Posted beats perfect. Volume is how you find what actually lands.

entries.caption:
Most people talk AT the camera. The ones who actually grow talk TO a person.

For the longest time my videos felt stiff — because I was performing for a lens. The second I started treating the camera like a client sitting across from me, everything changed. More watch time, more comments, more DMs that turned into real work.

Here's the exact shift 👇

1. Talk to ONE person — not "hey guys"
2. Say the point in the first line, or they're gone
3. Be yourself — your personality is the one thing nobody can copy
4. Make every video feel different
5. Stop overthinking it and just post

Save this for the next time you hit record. 📌

Follow @josephborroto for the stuff nobody tells you about content.

social.author: Joseph Borroto
social.headline: Stop trying to sound like a 'content creator.' Just be yourself on camera.
social.cta: Here's how I stay myself on camera →

slides.title: Talk how you actually talk
slides.body: The 'script voice' is what makes people scroll. Your real voice keeps them.

slides.title: Your quirks are the brand
slides.body: The weird way you say things is the one thing nobody can copy.

slides.title: Borrow structure, not personality
slides.body: Steal the format from big accounts. Keep your own voice on top of it.

slides.title: Film like you're texting a friend
slides.body: Casual beats polished. People trust a person, not a presenter.

slides.title: The more 'you,' the better it does
slides.body: Every time I loosen up on camera, the content does better.

entries.caption:
Stop trying to sound like a "content creator." Just talk.

My biggest unlock wasn't a better camera or a trending sound — it was dropping the fake "creator voice" and just being myself. People don't follow presenters. They follow people.

Here's how I keep it real on camera 👇

1. Talk how you actually talk
2. Your quirks ARE the brand
3. Borrow structure from big accounts — never their personality
4. Film like you're texting a friend
5. The more "you" it is, the better it does

Save this, then go be yourself on your next video. 📌

Follow @josephborroto for content tips that actually move the needle.

social.author: Joseph Borroto
social.headline: Most people overthink their content. I just get it out — and that's why mine grows.

slides.title: Posted beats perfect
slides.body: A 'good enough' video that exists beats a perfect one that never goes up.

slides.title: Volume teaches you
slides.body: You learn what works by posting, not by planning. The reps are the lesson.

slides.title: Lower the stakes
slides.body: One post isn't make-or-break. The hundredth one is what compounds.

slides.title: Batch when you can
slides.body: I filmed 12 videos on one trip — a week of content in an afternoon.

slides.title: Consistency compounds
slides.body: The algorithm rewards the person who keeps showing up. Be that person.

entries.caption:
Most people overthink their content into never posting it. I just get it out — and that's the whole secret.

Every "perfect" video sitting in your drafts is worth zero. The messy one you actually post is the one that grows you. Volume is how you learn what works.

My posting system 👇

1. Posted beats perfect — every time
2. Volume teaches you what planning can't
3. Lower the stakes: it's one post, not your reputation
4. Batch it — I shot 12 videos on a single trip
5. Consistency compounds. Keep showing up.

Save this for the days you don't feel like posting. 📌

Follow @josephborroto.

social.author: Joseph Borroto
social.headline: If your first line is weak, the rest of the video doesn't exist.

slides.title: Lead with the result
slides.body: Show the payoff first. Curiosity is what buys you the next 3 seconds.

slides.title: Call out one person
slides.body: "If you're a creator who…" — they can't scroll past themselves.

slides.title: Make a bold claim
slides.body: Say the thing most people are scared to say. Boring is invisible.

slides.title: Cut the warm-up
slides.body: No 'hey guys, so today.' Start ON the point, not before it.

slides.title: Test 3 hooks per idea
slides.body: Same video, three openings. Post the one that stops you first.

entries.caption:
Nobody owes you 3 seconds. Your first line has to earn them.

Here's the breakdown 👇

1. Lead with the result
2. Call out one person
3. Make a bold claim
4. Cut the warm-up
5. Test 3 hooks per idea

social.author: Joseph Borroto
social.headline: Stop over-editing. The cut should disappear, not show off.

slides.title: Cut the dead air
slides.body: Every 'um' and pause is an exit. Tighten until it's almost uncomfortable.

slides.title: One idea per cut
slides.body: If a clip isn't moving the story forward, it's slowing it down.

slides.title: Captions always
slides.body: Most people watch on mute. No captions = no message.

slides.title: Effects serve the point
slides.body: A zoom should land a line, not decorate it. Less is sharper.

slides.title: End on momentum
slides.body: Don't trail off. Cut on the strongest line so they rewatch.

entries.caption:
Good editing is invisible. People should feel the pace, not notice the cuts.

Here's the breakdown 👇

1. Cut the dead air
2. One idea per cut
3. Captions always
4. Effects serve the point
5. End on momentum

social.author: Joseph Borroto
social.headline: Posting once and quitting is why most people fail. Show up daily.

slides.title: Lower the bar to start
slides.body: Aim for 'posted,' not 'perfect.' Momentum beats motivation.

slides.title: Batch your filming
slides.body: Shoot a week in one sitting. Future you just posts.

slides.title: Keep an idea list
slides.body: Never stare at a blank page. Capture ideas the second they hit.

slides.title: Detach from one post
slides.body: No single video defines you. The body of work does.

slides.title: Show up on the bad days
slides.body: The post you don't feel like making is usually the one that hits.

entries.caption:
The algorithm doesn't reward talent. It rewards the person who keeps showing up.

Here's the breakdown 👇

1. Lower the bar to start
2. Batch your filming
3. Keep an idea list
4. Detach from one post
5. Show up on the bad days

Save this for later. 📌

Follow @josephborroto for more.

social.author: Joseph Borroto
social.headline: If your content is for everyone, it's for no one.

slides.title: Pick one person
slides.body: Make content for a specific human, not a vague audience.

slides.title: Own one topic
slides.body: Be the person known for ONE thing before you branch out.

slides.title: Speak their language
slides.body: Use the exact words your person uses. It feels made for them.

slides.title: Repeat your core idea
slides.body: You'll get bored before they do. Drill the same message new ways.

slides.title: Niche down to grow up
slides.body: A small, clear audience refers you. A broad, blurry one forgets you.

entries.caption:
Trying to reach everyone is the fastest way to reach no one.

Here's the breakdown 👇

1. Pick one person
2. Own one topic
3. Speak their language
4. Repeat your core idea
5. Niche down to grow up

Save this for later. 📌

Follow @josephborroto for more.

social.author: Joseph Borroto
social.headline: You don't need a better camera. You need a better first sentence.

slides.title: Message over gear
slides.body: A phone + a sharp idea beats a cinema camera + nothing to say.

slides.title: Hook before quality
slides.body: They decide in 1 second — long before they notice your lens.

slides.title: Lighting beats megapixels
slides.body: Face a window. Good light makes any camera look pro.

slides.title: Sound matters more than 4K
slides.body: People forgive a soft image. They won't forgive bad audio.

slides.title: Upgrade the idea first
slides.body: Buy the camera once the content is already working.

entries.caption:
People blame the camera. It's almost never the camera.

Here's the breakdown 👇

1. Message over gear
2. Hook before quality
3. Lighting beats megapixels
4. Sound over 4K
5. Upgrade the idea first

entries.alt_text: Carousel: gear doesn't make the content.

social.author: Joseph Borroto
social.headline: One good idea = 5 videos. Stop reinventing every post.

slides.title: Find your bangers
slides.body: The post that overperformed isn't done. It's a template.

slides.title: Change the angle
slides.body: Same idea, new hook. 'Why it works,' 'how to do it,' 'what I'd avoid.'

slides.title: Switch the format
slides.body: Turn a reel into a carousel into a single line. One idea, many shapes.

slides.title: Repost the winners
slides.body: Most of your audience never saw it. Run it back.

slides.title: Build a swipe file
slides.body: Keep your best ideas in one place so you never start from zero.

entries.caption:
Your best idea isn't a single post. It's a content engine.

Here's the breakdown 👇

1. Find your bangers
2. Change the angle
3. Switch the format
4. Repost the winners
5. Build a swipe file

Save this for later. 📌

Follow @josephborroto for more.
entries.alt_text: Carousel: repurpose one idea into many.

social.author: Joseph Borroto
social.headline: If you don't tell people what to do next, they won't.

slides.title: One ask per post
slides.body: Follow OR save OR comment. Pick one. Two asks = zero action.

slides.title: Make it effortless
slides.body: 'Comment ONE word.' The lower the effort, the higher the response.

slides.title: Tie it to the value
slides.body: 'Save this for your next video' beats a generic 'like and follow.'

slides.title: Earn it first
slides.body: Give something worth acting on before you ask for anything.

slides.title: Say it out loud
slides.body: Don't assume they'll figure it out. Tell them, clearly, once.

entries.caption:
Great content with no ask is a missed opportunity. Tell them what to do.

Here's the breakdown 👇

1. One ask per post
2. Make it effortless
3. Tie it to the value
4. Earn it first
5. Say it out loud

social.author: Joseph Borroto
social.headline: Your first 100 videos are practice. Post them anyway.

slides.title: Reps build the skill
slides.body: You can't think your way to good. You film your way there.

slides.title: Cringe is the toll
slides.body: Everyone's early stuff is rough. Pay it now, not later.

slides.title: Nobody's watching yet
slides.body: The small audience early is a gift — practice with the lights low.

slides.title: Track what lands
slides.body: Let the data, not your ego, tell you what's working.

slides.title: Stay in the game
slides.body: Most quit before the reps compound. Don't be most people.

entries.caption:
Your first 100 videos aren't the work. They're the warm-up.

Here's the breakdown 👇

1. Reps build the skill
2. Cringe is the toll
3. Nobody's watching yet
4. Track what lands
5. Stay in the game
